description: I’m interested in space exploration, technology, science, and game development. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, I’m excited to work on a Space Mission Design Game
summary:
**Orbital Odyssey – An Interactive Space Mission Simulation Game**

Orbital Odyssey is an interactive space mission simulation game that allows players to experience the challenges of planning, building, and executing space missions. Players take the role of a space mission commander, selecting missions such as Lunar Dash, Mars Express, and Orbital Rescue.

The game features a spacecraft customization workshop where players select engines, fuel tanks, power systems, protective hulls, and mission-specific payloads while managing limited credits, spacecraft mass, and thrust requirements. Players then launch their spacecraft and navigate through space, avoiding asteroids, collecting fuel and energy resources, and responding to unexpected events such as solar flares and micrometeoroid swarms.

An asteroid mining mini-game allows players to earn additional credits. Each mission provides rewards based on performance, encouraging strategic decisions and resource management.

Orbital Odyssey combines interactive gameplay with space engineering concepts to make space mission planning an engaging learning experience.
details:
Orbital Odyssey – Interactive Space Mission Simulation Game

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Orbital Odyssey is an interactive space mission simulation game that allows players to experience the challenges of planning, designing and executing space missions. Players take the role of a space mission commander and choose between three missions: Lunar Dash, Mars Express and Orbital Rescue.

Players enter a spacecraft workshop where they customize their spacecraft by selecting engines, fuel tanks, power systems, protective hulls and mission-specific payloads. Each component has different costs, mass, thrust, fuel capacity and durability. Players must balance these factors and stay within their available budget to build a spacecraft capable of completing the selected mission.

After passing the launch requirements, players navigate through space while managing resources and responding to unexpected events, including solar flares and micrometeoroid swarms. Players can make strategic decisions, protect their spacecraft and earn credits through successful missions and an asteroid mining mini-game.

2. What are the benefits?

The game makes complex space mission concepts more accessible and engaging. It encourages players to understand spacecraft components, resource limitations, engineering trade-offs, mission requirements and risk management through interactive gameplay rather than only theoretical explanations.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our aim is to increase interest in space exploration, aerospace engineering and STEM education. By allowing players to experiment with spacecraft configurations and experience the consequences of their decisions, Orbital Odyssey promotes curiosity, creativity, logical thinking and problem-solving skills.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed as a browser-based game using:

  • React: Building the interactive user interface and game components.
  • JavaScript: Implementing game logic, mission systems, resource management and interactions.
  • HTML: Structuring the web application.
  • CSS and Tailwind CSS: Designing the visual interface and styling the game.
  • Vite: Development environment and production build tool.
  • Lucide React: Icons and visual interface elements.
  • Browser Local Storage: Saving the player's credit balance between sessions.

The project runs in a web browser and does not require specialized hardware.

5. How is the project creative?

Orbital Odyssey combines spacecraft engineering and arcade-style space gameplay in a single interactive experience. Instead of simply presenting information about space missions, it allows players to make engineering decisions and immediately experience their consequences.

The combination of spacecraft customization, multiple mission objectives, random space events, resource management and asteroid mining creates an engaging experience that brings space mission planning into a game environment.

6. What factors did the team consider?

During development, we considered spacecraft mass, engine thrust, fuel consumption, power capacity, hull durability, payload requirements, available credits, mission difficulty and time limits.

We also considered gameplay accessibility, user engagement, balanced challenges and the importance of making engineering concepts understandable to players with different levels of space science knowledge.

Through Orbital Odyssey, we aim to make learning about space missions interactive, enjoyable and inspiring.

Our project, Orbital Odyssey, uses NASA's Near-Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs) API.

We integrated the NASA asteroid feed API (https://api.nasa.gov/neo/rest/v1/feed) to retrieve real near-Earth asteroid information for a seven-day period.

The game displays:

  • Asteroid names
  • Estimated maximum diameter
  • Close-approach dates
  • Distance from Earth
  • Potentially hazardous asteroid classification

Players can refresh the tracker to retrieve updated asteroid information. This NASA data integration helps connect the game's space exploration experience with real astronomical data.

NASA resource: NASA Near-Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs) – https://api.nasa.gov/
